rows.rule: The default property namespace is `zfs-endpoint:`; `-property-prefix democratic-csi` is adoption mode; a prefix is refused at startup unless every derived name is a valid OpenZFS user property (`a-z 0-9 - _ . :`, under 256 bytes with the suffix).

rows.type_idea: Configuration-dependent; run the ownership table under both prefixes.

rows.rule: For any request the planner accepts, a second identical CreateVolume succeeds, returns an identical Volume and performs zero zfs mutations (idempotency = empty plan).
rows.type_idea: Behavioural; FuzzCreateConverges never sets a content source, so clones are covered only by hand tests.

rows.rule: Capacity is rounded up to the effective volblocksize (requested, else configured default), never below the request; the returned capacity is >= required and <= limit.
rows.type_idea: `Bytes` type with checked `RoundUp(BlockSize)`; `BlockSize` only constructible as a power of two in [512,128K].

rows.rule: A limit-only request sets `refquota=limit`; it never creates an unlimited filesystem.
A rounded size above limit_bytes, or required > limit, is OutOfRange/InvalidArgument before any op.
rows.type_idea: `CapacityRange` constructor rejects required>limit; rounding check remains.

rows.rule: An incompatible re-create of a committed volume (larger size, other kind, limit below current, sparse vs thick, different properties) is AlreadyExists with no ops.
Capacity compatibility of a committed row: have >= required, and have <= limit when a limit is set; an unlimited filesystem (refquota 0, adopted) satisfies `required` when no limit is set.
The commit marker `provision_success=true` is the last op of every create plan; uncommitted rows are never listed or returned as volumes.
rows.type_idea: FSM cell `Ops` ends in `Commit`; `kindsMatch` assertion. Residual: per-cell check.

rows.rule: An owned uncommitted row (interrupted provision) is driven toward the request (sizes and properties set, then commit), not judged for compatibility.
Uncommitted volumes are not served: GetVolume, ExpandVolume, CreateSnapshot and PublishFileExport on an uncommitted row are NotFound (FSM I14).
rows.type_idea: Those planners take `CommittedVol`; only CreateVolume/Reconcile take `UncommittedVol`.

rows.rule: New filesystems get `sharenfs=off` and `sharesmb=off` set locally (a parent shared to `*` must not export them); zvols get no share properties.
rows.type_idea: Per-kind create-op structs: `CreateFS{Share ShareValue}` requires a share value, `CreateZvol` has none.

rows.rule: A thick zvol's `refreservation` is never hand-set (ZFS's zvol_auto_resv includes metadata and copies and tracks volsize); converging a thick zvol sets `refreservation=auto`.
rows.type_idea: `ZvolReservation` enum {Sparse, Auto}: there is no byte-valued reservation for zvols in the op vocabulary.

rows.rule: A sparse zvol has refreservation 0; `sparse` on a filesystem and `reserve` on a zvol are InvalidArgument.
rows.type_idea: Request is a sum type: `FSReq{Reserve}` | `ZvolReq{Sparse}`.

rows.rule: A filesystem with Reserve gets refreservation = refquota (including restores that take their size from the source).
Concurrent identical CreateVolumes serialize on the volume lock: all succeed and exactly one `zfs create` runs.
rows.type_idea: Concurrency.

rows.rule: A volume id is the CSI name: non-empty, <= 128 bytes, a valid zfs component with no `/` or `@`; an invalid name on CreateVolume is InvalidArgument.
rows.type_idea: `VolID` newtype, constructor `ParseName`; every planner takes `VolID`.

rows.rule: volblocksize: the requested value rounds volsize; a clone/restore keeps its origin's block size, so `-o volblocksize` is never passed to `zfs clone` and a mismatching request is InvalidArgument.
rows.type_idea: `Clone` op props type excludes create-only props (`CloneProps` subset of `Props`).

rows.rule: volblocksize cannot be converged on an uncommitted row: a mismatch is AlreadyExists; a match plans only the commit.
A block volume's device path is `/dev/zvol/<dataset>`; a filesystem's export path is its mountpoint.
Capacities above MaxInt64 are refused at the API boundary and size rounding never wraps (OutOfRange instead of a 1 MiB 'success').
rows.type_idea: `Bytes` is a checked uint63; `RoundUp` returns (Bytes, ok).

rows.rule: Restore from a snapshot honours growth (capacity = request) and records the content source (`csi_volume_content_source_type/id`); the Volume reports SourceType/SourceID.
Clone-from-volume cuts `<src>@volume-source-for-volume-<dst>`; the source cannot be deleted while the clone exists (FailedPrecondition); deleting the clone releases the internal snapshot.
A clone/restore whose source is larger than limit_bytes is OutOfRange before any op (no clone-source snapshot is cut), on every attempt.
A clone with capacity 0 takes the source's size (refquota, and with Reserve also refreservation); Reserve from an unlimited source is InvalidArgument.
A failure or crash after `zfs clone` converges on retry to the end state of an uninterrupted run (same refquota and refreservation, same response).
A request kind that differs from the source kind (filesystem request from a zvol snapshot) is InvalidArgument before any op, even when the source volume row is missing from the scan.
rows.type_idea: `CSISnap` carries its volume kind from decode.

rows.rule: A content source that is deferred-destroyed (deleted CSI snapshot) is NotFound.
rows.type_idea: StSnapCSIDeferred is not a `CSISnap` handle.

rows.rule: A content-source id the endpoint could never have issued, or that names nothing, is NotFound (never InvalidArgument).
rows.type_idea: ID parse returns `NeverIssued` variant mapped once.

rows.rule: A clone locks its source volume (and the source snapshot id for a restore) before scanning, so the source cannot be collected or deleted mid-clone.
rows.type_idea: Concurrency.

rows.rule: DeleteVolume of a missing volume is OK, and so is a second delete.
DeleteVolume refuses (FailedPrecondition) while a live (non-deferred) CSI snapshot exists, leaving every dataset unchanged.

DeleteVolume refuses (FailedPrecondition) a volume with a dependent clone, including a clone outside the parent (zfs `destroy_check_dependent` refuses before destroying anything; the snapshot `clones` property is the native reverse index).
rows.type_idea: Clones outside the scanned tree are invisible to any Table type.

rows.rule: A deferred (already deleted) CSI snapshot does not block its volume's delete or Reconcile.
rows.type_idea: StSnapCSIDeferred distinct state.

rows.rule: A deferred-destroyed snapshot survives while it has clones and is reaped when the last clone is destroyed (no leak).
rows.type_idea: Kernel semantics (dsl_destroy rmorigin).

rows.rule: A crash after any op of DeleteVolume converges on retry with no leaked clone-source snapshot (FSM CX1): order is `destroy -d` origin first, then each judged snapshot, then the dataset without `-r`.
rows.type_idea: FSM cell for Delete declares `Mid` states; per-cell crash test.

rows.rule: `dataset is busy` and `it's being held` on a destroy are FailedPrecondition (CSI 'in use').
rows.type_idea: Code keyed by (OpKind, Kind).

rows.rule: When the id's name is absent but a row with a local `csi_volume_name`/`csi_snapshot_name` equal to it exists (zfs rename/promote), Delete is FailedPrecondition naming the new location, never OK.
CreateSnapshot is idempotent for the same (name, source): same id, size and ready_to_use, no ops.
CSI snapshot names are global per endpoint: the same name on another volume is AlreadyExists (requires a whole-parent table).
rows.type_idea: PlanCreateSnapshot takes `WholeTable`.

rows.rule: Snapshot id is `<vol>@<name>` when the name is a valid component and the id fits 128 bytes, else `<vol>@csi-<32 hex of sha256(name)>`; an id still over 128 bytes is InvalidArgument; a retry re-finds the hashed snapshot.
rows.type_idea: `SnapID` newtype built only by `id(vol,name)`; residual: hash-collision/legacy table.

rows.rule: A snapshot name that is empty, over 128 bytes or contains control characters is InvalidArgument.
rows.type_idea: `SnapName` newtype.

rows.rule: A CSI snapshot name with the reserved prefix `volume-source-for-volume-` is InvalidArgument.
rows.type_idea: `SnapName` constructor refuses the prefix.

rows.rule: Snapshot delete uses `zfs destroy -d`: deleting a cloned snapshot succeeds, keeps the data, hides it from ListSnapshots, and zfs reaps it with the last clone.
rows.type_idea: `DestroySnap` op has no non-deferred form.

rows.rule: DeleteSnapshot of a missing, deferred or never-issued id is OK (requires a covering table).
DeleteSnapshot of a snapshot the endpoint did not make (admin, inherited markers, received) is FailedPrecondition and leaves it.
rows.type_idea: StSnapForeign error cell.

rows.rule: ListSnapshots lists only owned, non-deferred CSI snapshots.
rows.type_idea: Visibility derived from State.

rows.rule: CreateSnapshot whose name matches a deferred-destroyed CSI snapshot is AlreadyExists.
A snapshot's size is the volume size at snapshot time (a zvol snapshot keeps its volsize after the zvol grows).

Expanding an unlimited filesystem plans nothing, and the CSI response reports capacity_bytes = required (never 0).
node_expansion_required is true only for a zvol with a mount capability or no capability given; false for raw block and filesystems.

Expand never plans a volsize below the real one: a size cell zfs could not have printed (`-`, `none`, `1G`, negative, >2^64, not a volblocksize multiple) fails the scan as Internal instead of reading as 0.

rows.rule: ListVolumes pages in id order with max_entries and a next token; an unknown starting token is Aborted; negative max_entries is InvalidArgument.
ListVolumes returns only committed owned volumes (no uncommitted, foreign, received or aliased rows).
rows.type_idea: Visibility derived from State.

rows.rule: GetVolume of a missing volume is NotFound.
GetCapacity reports 0 when the requested capabilities or parameters could not be provisioned.

An id the endpoint could never have issued (full dataset path, > 128 bytes, `@` in a volume id) names nothing: DeleteVolume and DeleteSnapshot OK; GetVolume, Validate, Expand, CreateSnapshot source and CreateVolume source NotFound; an empty id stays InvalidArgument.

rows.rule: Only a classified not-found counts as absent; any unclassified error from Exists or a scan is an error, never absence.
rows.type_idea: Tri-state `Presence{Present,Absent,Unknown}` with no bool conversion.

rows.rule: A missing or exported pool or a missing parent is Unavailable on every RPC (single-volume and whole-parent scans), never NotFound or absent.
rows.type_idea: Sim-only today; real pool needs `zpool export`.

rows.rule: zfs stderr is classified from OpenZFS 2.4's own strings: exists, does not exist, parent does not exist, has children, has dependent clones, busy, being held, out of space, size greater than available, size less than used, pool read-only, key not loaded, must be one of, must be power of 2, pool must be upgraded, module does not support.

rows.rule: A zfs command killed by the caller's deadline or cancellation is ErrInterrupted carrying the context error (DeadlineExceeded/Aborted, never Internal); commands get SIGTERM then a bounded WaitDelay and return promptly.

rows.type_idea: Closed op sum type + exhaustive switch; unknown kind unrepresentable.

rows.rule: Every error returned after a mutation is in the sidecar in-progress set (Aborted, Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, ResourceExhausted), so a half-applied plan is always re-driven.

rows.rule: `parent does not exist` on create is Unavailable (the parent went away), not NotFound (which CSI reads as 'source missing', final).
Classification coverage of in-scope decisive OpenZFS stderr strings only rises (corpus ratchet per pinned 2.4.x tag).

rows.rule: zfs output is untrusted: a repeated (dataset, property) line fails the whole scan (user-property newline forgery).
rows.type_idea: JSON scan (`zfs get -j -p`) decoded into a map keyed by name: duplicates and forged lines are unrepresentable.

rows.rule: A forged line for a name zfs never printed (phantom row) cannot create a row.
rows.type_idea: Same JSON decode; with -Hp, grid check (P lines per block in request order).

rows.rule: A scan is all-or-nothing: a nonzero exit, a parse error or truncated output discards everything; no partial table reaches a planner.
rows.type_idea: Scan returns `(Table, error)` with Table only constructible after a clean end.

rows.rule: JSON scan uses `zfs get -j -p` (never `--json-int`, which drops leading zeros), runs with LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, and fails closed on JSON that zfs truncated with exit 0 (invalid UTF-8).
Numeric cells are strict: sizes must be decimal where the property applies to the row's type; zvol volsize > 0 and volsize % volblocksize == 0, else the scan fails.

rows.type_idea: `Kind` enum decoded jointly from (type, name); `Volumes()` iterates a typed slice.

rows.rule: Impossible rows fail the scan: readonly props with a source other than `-`, a quota-family `0` not sourced `default`, `inherited from` on PROP_DEFAULT props, origin on a non-clone, space bounds violated.
rows.type_idea: Decoder rules as a data table.

rows.rule: A user property literally set to `-` with source local is a real value, not 'unset'.
rows.type_idea: `Prop{Set bool; Value string}` instead of '' sentinel (JSON gives this for free).

rows.rule: Rows deeper than a volume are kept as that volume's dependents, never dropped.
rows.type_idea: Table carries `Dependents(vol)`.

rows.rule: A Table records its coverage (whole parent or the volumes scanned); planners that conclude from absence (delete missing, free name, unique snapshot name, reconcile, export) refuse an uncovered table with Internal.
rows.type_idea: `WholeTable` vs `ScopedTable` types; absence-acting planners take `WholeTable` or a `Covered[VolID]` proof.

rows.rule: Names zfs accepts but the endpoint cannot address (space, leading `_`) are marked and skipped with a reason, never targeted, and never abort a reconcile.
rows.type_idea: Decode yields `Unaddressable` rows that have no `Target`.

rows.rule: The zfs client refuses flag-like and shell-meta dataset names and newlines in property values before exec, and never uses a shell.
rows.type_idea: `DatasetName` newtype; runner takes `[]Arg` built from typed values.

rows.rule: Index properties print as the first table name (2.4 tables): gzip-6 -> gzip, zstd-fast-1 -> zstd-fast, posixacl -> posix, xattr on -> sa, snapdir=disabled valid, snapdir=shown refused.
rows.type_idea: Sim fidelity; oracle is zfs_prop.c 2.4 or a real pool.

rows.rule: Simulator lifecycle matches zfs: create of an existing dataset ErrExists; destroy of a cloned snapshot HasClones; `-d` keeps it until the last clone; sparse zvol refreservation 0; user properties set at create are `local`.

Property passthrough is default-deny: mountpoint, sharenfs, sharesmb, canmount, exec, setuid, devices, key*/encryption, quota family, volsize, readonly, zoned, every user property (including ownership markers), non-allowlisted natives, wrong case and empty keys are InvalidArgument before state is read, and nothing is created.
rows.type_idea: Request carries `map[AllowedProp]Value` where `AllowedProp` is a closed enum parsed at the API edge.

rows.rule: Per-kind masks: recordsize, atime, relatime, xattr, acltype, snapdir are filesystem-only; volblocksize and copies are zvol-only (copies on a filesystem counts against refquota and would silently cut capacity).
rows.type_idea: `FSProp` and `ZvolProp` separate enums.

rows.type_idea: Per-prop value enums generated from zfs_prop.c 2.4.

rows.rule: Requested properties are applied locally at create (`create -o`, `clone -o`) and read back equal to their canonical form.

A committed volume is compatible only if each requested property is set locally with the same canonical value; unrequested local properties are not compared; default/inherited is not local; volblocksize is compared by effective value.
An uncommitted row converges properties by setting only the differing ones, then commits.
OpenZFS 2.4 is the only supported version: 2.4 value spellings only (xattr dir/on and snapdir=disabled differ on 2.2); the daemon refuses to start unless userland and kmod are both zfs-2.4.*.
CSI StorageClass parameters: only `sparse` and `reserve` (booleans) are accepted, `csi.storage.k8s.io/*` keys are dropped before the endpoint; any other key or a non-bool is InvalidArgument.

rows.type_idea: `CanonicalShare` built from `[]netip.Prefix`; render(parse(x)) == x round-trip is the only test.

Publish of the same client in the same mode runs no `zfs set`; the other mode is AlreadyExists; Unpublish of an absent client, of a missing volume, of a zvol, and a repeated Unpublish are OK; publish/unpublish sequences converge.

Export clients are IPv4 addresses/CIDRs only: empty, `*`, netgroups, IPv6, option text, shell metacharacters, `0.0.0.0/0`, prefixes below the floor, hex/octal aliases and leading zeros are InvalidArgument; no hostnames (DNS failure silently revokes).

rows.type_idea: `SetShare{NoMount bool}` required field derived from Mounted.

rows.rule: sharenfs is limited to 8191 bytes (ZAP_MAXVALUELEN - 1); a longer value is ResourceExhausted before any set.
rows.type_idea: `CanonicalShare` constructor checks length.

rows.rule: File export is advertised and served only when enabled (root); otherwise the capability is absent and both RPCs are Unimplemented.

Static export at create: `zfs create -o sharenfs=<canonical>`, verify nfsd and etab, and only then set the commit marker (committed means created and served); a crash at C1-C5 is recoverable from sharenfs, etab and the marker alone.
Root squash stays on: the endpoint sets the new dataset root's owner and mode from StorageClass parameters before committing.

The inherited-sharenfs window: a dataset without a local sharenfs inherits a shared parent's value (`on` = rw,crossmnt to `*`); the first publish pins a local value and `*` is no longer served; the parent's effective sharenfs must be `off` at startup so a crash inside the create ioctl (props not yet set) exports nothing.
rows.source: internal/endpoint/export_contract_test.go:228; internal/endpoint/export_test.go:605; scratchpad/wave6/csi-nfs-design.md Fact A, B, C1
rows.type_idea: Only real libshare + nfsd show the `*` export.

rows.rule: Unsafe sharenfs forms (`rw=`, `rw=a::b`, `rw=a:`, bare rw/ro, `on`) export to the world; the endpoint never writes them and reconcile reports `world-export`.
rows.type_idea: `CanonicalShare` cannot render an empty host (non-empty sorted list).

rows.rule: Overlapping clients are banned: mountd takes the first matching export (FQDN before subnet, then file order), so a ro /32 inside a rw /24 would be served rw.
rows.type_idea: `CanonicalShare` constructor rejects overlap.

rows.rule: A node_id used as an export client must be one IPv4 host (`/32`), never a CIDR; Unpublish with an empty node_id unpublishes all (MANAGED value -> off).
rows.type_idea: `NodeHost` newtype (single /32).

rows.rule: Reconcile reports export drift D1-D7 (inherited, foreign/world-export/below-floor, not-served/extra-served, nfsd-down, parent-shared, orphan-export, legacy nfs_clients); its only export write is a reshare of an unchanged MANAGED value.
Deleting an exported filesystem needs no explicit unshare: `zfs destroy` unshares, runs exportfs, unmounts and destroys; a busy unmount re-shares and fails, leaving the volume unchanged.
volume_context carries `server` (one of the advertised -nfs-server entries) and `share` (the mountpoint); publish_context stays empty; the export RPC returns the bare export path.
Reconcile only destroys, replay-tolerantly (OkMissing); snapshots are destroyed deferred (`-d`), volumes are not.
rows.type_idea: `ReconcileAction` holds a `Destroy` op variant only.

rows.rule: Reconcile never targets unowned, received or renamed rows, desired volumes, CSI snapshots, volumes with CSI snapshots, rows younger than MinAge, or rows with unknown creation.
rows.type_idea: Candidate filter = FSM cells; residual: property test.

rows.rule: An empty desired set collects no committed volume (skipped with SkipEmptyDesired) but still collects old uncommitted rows.
rows.type_idea: `Desired` sum type {Unknown, Set(nonempty)}.

rows.rule: A desired set naming no existing volume is treated like an empty one, and destructive runs are bounded (max_deletions, or a dry-run plan digest the real run must echo).
Uncommitted rows older than MinAge are collected (abandoned creates); younger ones are skipped as possibly in flight; a desired uncommitted row is left for the caller's retry.

MinAge counts from commit for committed rows (max(creation, committed_at)), has a floor, and the locked re-plan may only drop actions from the unlocked plan, never add or reclassify (SkipChangedSinceScan).
rows.type_idea: Race between commit and reconcile.

rows.rule: Fixpoint: a clone, its clone-source snapshot and the freed source are collected in one run, clone first; a young clone blocks the chain with reasons.
rows.type_idea: simulateDestroy is a second model of dsl_destroy; oracle must be zfs.

rows.rule: Orphan clone-source snapshots (clone gone) are collected; one in use is kept; one on an unowned volume is reported only; a young one is skipped as mid-clone.
A dry run returns the plan as data, applies nothing and takes no locks; with nothing changing, it equals the real run's plan.
Reconcile locks every target and the clone each released source serves; a target held by another operation is not destroyed (Aborted today; per-group skip decided).
rows.type_idea: Action type carries its lock set; apply takes `Locked[Action]`.

rows.rule: A second reconcile with the same request plans nothing.
One failing destroy neither hides what already ran nor starves later candidates: apply per candidate group, report failures as skips, return the partial plan.
Reconcile input: an invalid desired id is InvalidArgument; min_age_seconds that overflows is InvalidArgument; 0 means the default of one hour.
Every skip carries its reason (desired missing, too young, no creation, empty desired, has snapshot X, dependent clone Y, unmanaged source, foreign snapshots named, changed since scan).
rows.type_idea: Reason is a closed enum + detail.

rows.rule: Garbage collection runs only on demand against a caller-supplied desired set, off the request path; request RPCs never consult a desired-state store.
rows.type_idea: No desired-state type reachable from request planners.

rows.rule: Every resource an operation touches is locked (volume, a clone's source volume and snapshot, clone-source owners) with keys taken in sorted order (no deadlock).
rows.type_idea: Planner returns its lock set; apply refuses a plan whose targets are outside it.

rows.rule: A mutation never consumes a scan that started before it took its locks (single-flight sharing is for List* only).
rows.type_idea: `LockedScan` token produced only by scan-after-lock.

rows.rule: One endpoint instance per parent per host: a per-parent flock; a second instance on the same parent is refused ('already manages').
The unix socket is 0600 in a 0700 directory; a live socket is refused, a stale one replaced, and a non-socket (file, directory, symlink) at the path is never deleted.
No unauthenticated TCP listener serves the destructive API (until ADR 0001 mTLS).
zfs children run in their own process group with a parent-death signal; shutdown drains in-flight zfs within -drain, then kills leftovers.
Every destroy plan is written to the audit log (principal, rpc, targets) before it is applied.
Planners are pure: (Table, request) in, Plan or typed error out; no I/O, no clock except an injected Now.
rows.type_idea: Planner signatures take no ctx/Runner; package boundary forbids importing the runner.

rows.rule: After a successful mutating RPC, re-observing and re-planning the same request under the same locks yields an empty plan (verification = residual plan).
rows.type_idea: Same-model blindness: re-plan agrees with a misread (future.md §4.4).

rows.rule: Plans are printable, diffable data with golden tests (one fat Op struct or closed variants with String()).
A crash or kill after any op k of any plan, followed by the CO's retry, ends in the same state and response as the uninterrupted run (DeleteVolume CX1 still open).
rows.type_idea: Oracle is the uncrashed run of the same code: common-mode.

rows.rule: A kill in the middle of a multi-property `zfs set` (any proper subset applied) converges on retry.
`zfs destroy -r` is not atomic: children and snapshots go first, in post-order, before a later failure; a held snapshot does not protect the rest of the tree.
`zfs create`/`clone` with `-o` props is atomic with respect to invalid props (the ioctl destroys the new objset if setting props fails) but not with the share/mount step, which fails with exit 0.
The controller advertises exactly CREATE_DELETE_VOLUME, CREATE_DELETE_SNAPSHOT, LIST_VOLUMES, LIST_SNAPSHOTS, GET_CAPACITY, CLONE_VOLUME, EXPAND_VOLUME (no PUBLISH_UNPUBLISH).

MULTI_NODE_MULTI_WRITER is InvalidArgument at create; ValidateVolumeCapabilities confirms only supported capabilities (zvol: block and mount; reserved filesystem: mount only) and returns NotFound for unknown ids.
rows.type_idea: Static-NFS mode changes this (all five modes for FILESYSTEM, csi-nfs-design §7).

rows.rule: volume_context `kind` is `filesystem` or `block` matching the endpoint kind.
csi-sanity's Identity and Controller groups pass on the simulator and on real ZFS in both access types; the focus regex is unanchored and a spec-count floor fails a run that executes 0 specs.
The front end passes endpoint gRPC codes through unchanged and propagates deadlines, so the sidecar sees ABORTED/UNAVAILABLE/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED as produced.
ValidateVolumeCapabilities confirms parameters and volume_context only after checking them against the volume.
Each request runs one scan per source (one `zfs get`) and decodes it once into an immutable Table.
rows.type_idea: Planner input structs hold one `Table` value; counted via Sim.Calls.

rows.rule: DeleteVolume scans only the volume's subtree (zfs refuses dependent clones itself); CreateSnapshot's global-name check reads only snapshots and 3 columns.
PlanReconcile is linear in rows (one-pass simulateDestroyAll): 16k volumes plan in well under a second (31 s -> 86 ms measured).
Concurrent full-parent scans are single-flighted (List* only) and bounded by a 1-2 slot semaphore; zfs execs are bounded overall.
p99 latency of every RPC stays under 5 s (half the 10 s sidecar timeout) at 10k datasets / 100k snapshots on real ZFS.
The scan decoder streams with all-or-nothing return and narrows columns and types per operation; Go-side cost per 10k rows is measured, not inferred (README:71's 12 us claim is falsified: ~230 ms).
